# Repository metadata (for GitHub "About" + settings)

These aren't applied automatically — paste them into your repo's settings on github.com.

## Description (Settings → top of repo → About ✎)

> A beginner-to-expert, open-source course on Large Language Models & Semantic Search —
> keyword search, embeddings, dense retrieval, vector databases, re-ranking, hybrid search,
> evaluation, and RAG — with intuitive lessons, runnable notebooks, and a free e-book.

Short version (if the field is tight):

> Beginner-to-expert course on LLMs & semantic search: embeddings, dense retrieval, re-ranking, RAG — with notebooks and a free e-book.

## Website (About → Website field)

Point at the e-book or your GitHub Pages site if you publish one.

## Topics (About → Topics)

```
semantic-search, information-retrieval, embeddings, dense-retrieval, rag,
retrieval-augmented-generation, vector-database, faiss, bm25, reranking,
sentence-transformers, nlp, machine-learning, large-language-models, course,
tutorial, education, python
```

## Social preview image (Settings → General → Social preview → Upload)

Upload `assets/social-preview.png` (1280×640). This is the thumbnail shown when the repo is
shared on social media, chat, and search.

## Suggested first release

- Tag: `v1.0.0`  →  `git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Search Semantically v1.0.0" && git push --tags`
- Release title: **Search Semantically v1.0.0**
- Attach `Search-Semantically-ebook.pdf` as a release asset.
- Use the `CHANGELOG.md` v1.0.0 section as the release notes.
